questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the principle of safe blood transfusion?

options.a: The donor's red blood corpuscles should not contain antibodies against the recipient's serum.
options.b: The recipient's serum should not contain antigens against the donor's antibodies.
options.c: The recipients serum should not contain the antibodies against the antigens present on red blood corpuscles of the donor
options.d: The recipient's red blood corpuscles should not contain antibodies against the donor's antigen.

questions.solution: (c) The recipients serum should not contain the antibodies against the antigens present on red blood corpuscles of the donor. If recipient plasma has antibodies against donor RBC antigens, the donor cells agglutinate.

questions.question: Aruna went to a theatre to watch a movie on a bright sunny morning. As she came out of the theatre, she felt a dazzling effect and could not open her eyes. After a few minutes, her vision became normal. This is due to,
questions.solution: (d) Adaptation of the eye. Light adaptation: the pupil constricts and rhodopsin bleaches so the eye adjusts to bright light.

questions.question: Variegated leaf experiment is carried out to test the presence of ____.
questions.solution: (b) Chlorophyll. A variegated leaf shows that chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis (only green parts form starch).

questions.question: Ajay and Vijay are siblings. Ajay can roll his tongue while Vijay cannot. What is the genotype of their parents?

options.a: Both the parents are homozygous dominant
options.b: Both the parents are homozygous recessive
options.c: One parent is homozygous dominant, and the other parent is homozygous recessive
options.d: Both the parents are heterozygous dominant.

questions.solution: (d) Both the parents are heterozygous dominant.. A non-roller child (rr) needs an r from each parent, and a roller child shows R is present; of the options, only heterozygous (Rr x Rr) parents can give both.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about lymph?
P- Lymph is colourful as it has haemoglobin but no RBC.
Q- It contains platelets responsible for clotting.
R- Lymph is an important carrier for nutrients and hormones.
S- Fats are absorbed through the lymph in the lacteals present in the intestinal villi.
questions.solution: (b) R and S. Lymph is colourless (no haemoglobin) and lacks platelets; it carries nutrients/hormones and absorbs fats via lacteals.

questions.question:
Statement 1: Family welfare centres have an inverted red triangle sign.
Statement 2: The centre deals with subsequent care of the children, e.g., immunisation, and oral rehydration therapy to ensure survival of the young ones.

options.c: Statement 1 is true, statement 2 is false
options.d: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true

questions.solution: (a) Both the statements are true.. The inverted red triangle is the family welfare symbol, and these centres also provide child care such as immunisation and ORT.

questions.question:
Assertion: The arrangement of white and gray matter is the same in both brain and spinal cord.
Reason: Gray matter consists of cell bodies of neurons.

options.a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.b: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.c: Assertion is true, Reason is false.
options.d: Assertion is false, Reason is true

questions.solution: (d) Assertion is false, Reason is true. In the brain grey matter is outside (cortex) and white matter inside; in the spinal cord it is reversed. So the Assertion is false; the Reason is true.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question: If you begin with one cell and follow it through four mitotic divisions, then how many daughter cells would be there?
questions.solution: (d) 16. Each division doubles the cells: 2^4 = 16.

questions.question: Usually a recessive character is expressed only when present in a homozygous recessive condition. However, a single recessive gene can express itself in human beings when the gene is present on

options.d: either on autosome or on X chromosome

questions.solution: (a) X chromosome of male. Males have a single X (hemizygous), so one recessive X-linked allele is expressed.

questions.question: On stimulation, a nerve fibre which is in resting stage becomes

options.c: equally permeable to Na and K+

questions.solution: (a) more permeable to Na+. Stimulation opens sodium channels; Na+ rushes in causing depolarisation.

questions.question: In tea plantations and hedge making, gardeners trim the plants regularly so that they remain bushy. Scientific explanation behind this is:
questions.solution: (d) both a and b. Trimming removes the auxin-producing apex (apical dominance), so lateral buds grow and the plant becomes bushy.

questions.question:
A teacher asked the students to give two examples of substances that pass from mother to foetus. Which students have given the correct answer?
Student 1- Oxygen and glucose
Student 2- Oxygen and urea
Student 3- Amino acid and vitamins
Student 4- Carbon dioxide and glucose
questions.solution: (c) Student 1 and 3. Oxygen, glucose, amino acids and vitamins pass mother -> foetus; urea and CO2 pass foetus -> mother.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question:
Assertion: Both centromere and centrosome are parts of a chromosome.
Reason: The centromere is the region where spindle fibres attach, while the centrosome helps in formation of spindle fibres.

options.a: Assertion is true and Reason is false
options.b: Assertion is false and Reason is true.
options.c: Both Assertion and Reason are true
options.d: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

questions.solution: (b) Assertion is false and Reason is true.. The centrosome is a cytoplasmic organelle (centrioles), not part of a chromosome, so the Assertion is false; the Reason is true.

questions.question:
Choose the option which gives the correct sequence of events during urination.
P- Urinary bladder sends signals to the CNS
Q- The bladder fills with urine and becomes distended
R- Micturition
S- CNS passes on impulses for relaxation of urethral sphincter
questions.solution: (c) Q-P-S-R. The bladder distends, stretch signals go to the CNS, the CNS relaxes the sphincter, then micturition occurs.

questions.chapter: Cell Cycle and Structure of Chromosomes
questions.question:
Read the following statements.
P- In mitotic cell division chromosome number is halved.
Q- Nuclear membrane and nucleolus disappear during prophase.
R- The period between two successive mitotic divisions is known as telophase.
S- In the G2 phase of the cell cycle, proteins are synthesized.
Which of the above given statements are correct?
questions.solution: (d) Q and S. Mitosis keeps the chromosome number constant (P wrong); the period between divisions is interphase (R wrong).

questions.question: Distinguish between: Sewage and Effluents (Explanation)
questions.solution: Sewage: waste water from homes (kitchens, toilets, bathrooms) containing human excreta, detergents and organic matter. Effluents: liquid wastes discharged from industries/factories containing chemicals, heavy metals, etc.

questions.question: Distinguish between: Natality and Mortality (Definition)
questions.solution: Natality: number of live births per 1000 individuals per year. Mortality: number of deaths per 1000 individuals per year.

questions.topic: Posture of Homo habilis vs Homo sapiens sapiens
concepts: Posture of Homo habilis vs Homo sapiens sapiens
questions.question: Distinguish between: Homo habilis and Homo sapiens sapiens (Posture)
questions.solution: Homo habilis: erect but slightly stooped/semi-erect posture. Homo sapiens sapiens: fully erect posture.

questions.question: Distinguish between: Active transport and Osmosis (Significance)
questions.solution: Active transport: enables absorption of mineral ions by root hairs against the concentration gradient (using energy/ATP). Osmosis: enables absorption of water by root hairs from the soil and maintains cell turgidity.

questions.question: Distinguish between: Lubb and Dup (Cause of sound)
questions.solution: Lubb: caused by the closure of the atrioventricular (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves at the start of ventricular systole. Dup: caused by the closure of the semilunar valves at the start of ventricular diastole.

questions.solution: Emission standards (e.g. Bharat Stage norms) set legal limits on pollutants (CO, NOx, hydrocarbons, particulates) released by vehicles, thereby reducing air pollution and protecting health.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Lee, an athlete, was told that diuretics are banned in all sports by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA). What are diuretics? Which hormone in our body controls diuresis?
questions.solution: Diuretics are substances (drugs, also tea/coffee/alcohol) that increase the volume of urine produced. Diuresis is controlled by the antidiuretic hormone (ADH / vasopressin) secreted by the posterior pituitary.

questions.question:
A moisture gradient was created in soil by watering only one side of a pot. After a few days, roots grow towards the wet side, even against gravity.
a) Which tropic response is observed here?
b) Define tropism.
questions.solution: (a) Positive hydrotropism. (b) Tropism is the directional growth movement of a plant part in response to an external stimulus coming from a particular direction.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
An experiment was set up as shown in the figure below. (Figure: a potted destarched plant in sunlight; Leaf 1 is enclosed in a bottle/flask A containing KOH, held by a split cork; Leaf 2 is outside on the same plant.)
a) What is the aim of the experiment?
b) The set up has been exposed to sunlight for two days. What will be the observation, if you perform an iodine test on Leaf 1 and 2? Why?
questions.solution: (a) To show that carbon dioxide is necessary for photosynthesis (Moll's half-leaf type experiment). (b) Leaf 1 (inside the flask) does not turn blue-black - no starch, because KOH absorbs CO2 so no photosynthesis occurs. Leaf 2 (outside) turns blue-black - starch present, because it received CO2 and carried out photosynthesis.

marking_points.point: (b) Leaf 1 no blue-black, KOH absorbs CO2

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Explain the term plasmolysis. Give one application of this phenomenon in our daily lives.
questions.solution: Plasmolysis: shrinkage of the protoplasm of a plant cell away from the cell wall due to loss of water by exosmosis when placed in a hypertonic solution. Application: salting of pickles / sugaring of jams preserves food (microbes get plasmolysed); or killing weeds by salting; or salt sprinkled on leeches/snails.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Draw a Punnet square to find out the progeny of a marriage between a colourblind man and a carrier woman.
questions.solution:
Colourblind man: XcY; carrier woman: XXc.
Gametes - man: Xc, Y; woman: X, Xc.
Punnet square: X x Xc = XXc (carrier daughter); Xc x Xc = XcXc (colourblind daughter); X x Y = XY (normal son); Xc x Y = XcY (colourblind son).
Result: 25% carrier daughters, 25% colourblind daughters, 25% normal sons, 25% colourblind sons (50% of daughters and 50% of sons colourblind).

questions.solution: Any two: about 1.8 m tall with fully erect posture; cranial capacity about 1600 cc; prominent chin, broad face and high, vertical forehead; no supraorbital (eyebrow) ridges; reduced jaws and teeth.

questions.question: What is the function of thrombokinase?
questions.solution: Thrombokinase (thromboplastin), released by injured tissues and platelets, converts prothrombin into thrombin in the presence of calcium ions.

questions.question: Kathak is an Indian classical dance which involves a lot of spinning by the dancers. After the spins, the dancers usually feel dizzy. Name the parts in the ear responsible for dynamic equilibrium and static balance.
questions.solution: Dynamic equilibrium: semicircular canals (ampullae). Static balance: vestibule (utriculus and sacculus).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give any two protective functions of the blood.
questions.solution: Any two: WBCs (neutrophils, monocytes) engulf germs by phagocytosis; lymphocytes produce antibodies; clotting prevents blood loss and entry of germs at wounds; antitoxins neutralise toxins.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B

They have photoreceptor cells similar to humans which enable dim light vision. Name the photoreceptor cell and the pigment it contains, which aids them in night vision.
questions.solution: Rod cells; pigment rhodopsin (visual purple).

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: As an informed citizen of the new era, how will you explain sustainable development? Elaborate on the 3R's in the context of sustainable development.
questions.solution: Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. 3Rs: Reduce - cut down consumption and waste (e.g. save water/electricity, avoid plastics). Reuse - use items again (e.g. glass jars, cloth bags). Recycle - reprocess waste into new products (e.g. paper, plastic, metal recycling), conserving resources and reducing pollution.

questions.solution: Any one: to increase the size of fruits like grapes and produce seedless fruits (parthenocarpy); to increase stem length of sugarcane (more yield); to break seed dormancy / promote malting in brewing.

a) Name any two gaseous pollutants produced due to extensive industrialization.

questions.solution: (a) Any two: sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide (also hydrocarbons). (b) Any two: chronic respiratory diseases such as asthma, bronchitis; lung cancer; cardiovascular (heart) diseases; eye irritation.

questions.question:
A dog breeder crossed a purebred black coated labrador(BB) with a chocolate coated labrador(bb). All the puppies were black coated. The breeder then crossed two of these F1 puppies and observed that some F2 puppies were chocolate coated.
a) Which law of Mendel is illustrated when all the F1 offspring are black?
b) What is the expected phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation?
questions.solution: (a) Law of dominance. (b) Bb x Bb gives 3 black : 1 chocolate.

Observe the image given and answer the following questions.
a) Name the process.
b) Why does this process take place in certain plants?
c) Give 2 examples of plants wherein this process is commonly observed.
questions.solution: (a) Guttation. (b) When root pressure is high and transpiration is low (humid nights/early morning with moist soil), excess water is forced out as droplets through hydathodes at the leaf margins. (c) Any two: grass, tomato, Colocasia (arum), Nasturtium, garden balsam.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A cleanliness campaign was launched by the Government of India on 2nd October 2014, with certain goals in mind.
a) Name the programme.
b) Mention any two objectives curated by the Government which could lead us to achieve those goals.
questions.solution: (a) Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission). (b) Any two: eliminate open defecation by building toilets; scientific solid waste management; clean streets, roads and public places; create awareness about sanitation and hygiene.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Explain the fate of corpus luteum under each of the following situations
a) On fertilization
b) In case of no fertilization
questions.solution: (a) It persists and keeps secreting progesterone, maintaining the uterine lining for pregnancy (until the placenta takes over). (b) It degenerates (into corpus albicans); progesterone falls and menstruation follows.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: When is albumin passed out in the urine? Name this condition.
questions.solution: Albumin appears in urine when the glomeruli are damaged/inflamed (kidney disease, high blood pressure) so plasma proteins leak through. The condition is called albuminuria.

marking_points.point: When glomerular filtration membrane is damaged

questions.question:
Given below is a sectional view of the human brain. Study the figure and answer the following questions.
a) Name the part labelled as p and q.
b) Give the function of the part labelled s.
c) What is the functional relation between parts labelled p and q?
questions.solution: (a) p - Cerebrum; q - Corpus callosum. (b) s - Pons: relays impulses between the medulla/cerebellum and cerebrum and helps regulate breathing. (c) The corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres and transfers information between them so they work in coordination.

questions.question: What is parthenocarpy?
questions.solution: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits (e.g. induced by gibberellins/auxins).

questions.topic: Beyond syllabus: Girdling and phloem translocation
concepts: Beyond syllabus: Girdling and phloem translocation
questions.question:
The figure below represents a tree in which a ring of bark was removed. After a few weeks, a swelling appeared on the bark above the ring while the bark below shrivelled up.
a) Give a reason for the swelling in the bark above the ring.
b) Why is there a shrinkage of the bark below the ring?
questions.solution: (a) Removing the ring of bark removes the phloem; food made in the leaves moving downward through phloem accumulates above the ring, causing swelling. (b) Food cannot reach the tissues below the ring, so they are starved and shrivel.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Oscar is collecting information related to the ozone layer. Help him with the cause and the process which leads to breakdown of the ozone layer.
questions.solution: Cause: chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerators, ACs and aerosols (also halons, NOx). Process: in the stratosphere UV rays break CFCs releasing free chlorine atoms; each Cl atom reacts with ozone (Cl + O3 -> ClO + O2) and is regenerated, destroying thousands of ozone molecules, thinning the ozone layer.

marking_points.point: Process: UV releases Cl which breaks O3 to O2

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Liza visited the doctor for a complete health checkup. After the checkup, following readings were displayed for her on the sphygmomanometer: 120/80.
a) What does this reading represent? Elaborate.
b) What do the numbers 120 and 80 indicate? At what point in the cycle of the heart beat do we get these readings?
questions.solution: (a) It is her blood pressure - the pressure exerted by blood on the walls of the arteries, measured in mm Hg; 120/80 is normal BP. (b) 120 mm Hg is the systolic pressure - recorded during ventricular systole (contraction). 80 mm Hg is the diastolic pressure - recorded during ventricular diastole (relaxation).
